ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There are four cards on the table as in the picture. Every card has a letter on one side and a number on the other side. Peter said: "For every card on the table it is true that if there is a vowel on one side, there is an even number on the other side." What is the smallest number of cards Alice must turn in order to check whether Peter said the truth?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The picture shows visible card faces with the symbols E, K, 4, 6, and 7. E and K are letters; 4, 6, and 7 are numbers. E is a vowel, K is a consonant, 4 and 6 are even numbers, and 7 is an odd number. Reasoning: Peter's statement is the conditional rule: if a card has a vowel on one side, then it has an even number on the other side. To check whether this rule is false, Alice only needs to look for possible counterexamples: a vowel with an odd number on the other side. Therefore, she must turn over the E card to check that its hidden number is even. She must also turn over the 7 card to check that its hidden letter is not a vowel. Turning over K is unnecessary because a consonant does not test the rule. Turning over 4 or 6 is unnecessary because even numbers cannot disprove the rule, regardless of the hidden letter. So the smallest number of cards Alice must turn is 2.
